Hmm, let me think about this hand. I've got two lands (Ancient Tomb and Urza's Saga), which is good for mana acceleration, but I'm seeing some expensive cards here. The One Ring at 4 mana, Fury at 5 mana, and another Fury at 5 mana. Blood Moon at 3 mana is solid, and Pyrogoyf at 4 mana.

Back in my day, we kept hands like this and made them work! But this is a bit clunky - I need more early game action. With only two lands and mostly 4+ mana spells, this could be too slow. I think I need to mulligan this one and hope for a better curve.

I'll lead with a fetchland. Flooded Strand gives me access to Underground Sea, which is perfect for casting my cantrips and rituals. The flexibility to grab either Island or Plains-equivalent (Underground Sea/Volcanic Island) is valuable.

I'll take the mulligan down to 6 cards. Back in my day, we didn't have these fancy mulligan rules - you kept what you drew and you liked it! But I've got to adapt with the times, and that hand was just too slow for this young whippersnapper's format.

annotations.description: Leading with Ancient Tomb over Urza's Saga is debatable. Urza's Saga on turn 1 gets the lore counter rolling, provides colorless mana on the same turn, and starts building toward the chapter III tutor or chapter II construct tokens. Ancient Tomb deals 2 damage each time it's tapped. With Blood Moon in hand, there's an argument for Ancient Tomb (tap for 2 colorless, then play Urza's Saga next turn before Blood Moon turns it into a Mountain on turn 2-3). However, the player has Simian Spirit Guide in hand, so a strong line would be: Turn 1 Urza's Saga (gets lore counter I, can tap for {C}), Turn 2 Ancient Tomb + Simian Spirit Guide exile = {C}{C} + {R} = Blood Moon on turn 2, locking the opponent's Flooded Strand. Playing Ancient Tomb first delays Urza's Saga's saga counter progression by a turn. That said, Ancient Tomb first does allow a turn 2 Blood Moon with just Ancient Tomb + SSG (tap Tomb for {C}{C} + exile SSG for {R}), which is the same speed. The key difference is Urza's Saga gets its counters ticking sooner. Since Blood Moon will eventually destroy Urza's Saga by making it a Mountain (losing its saga abilities), the sequencing around Blood Moon matters. Overall this is close but leading Urza's Saga may have been slightly better to start the saga clock.

annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Pyrogoyf, allowing it to resolve with its 5-damage ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Cast Daze (returning Island to hand) to counter Pyrogoyf while opponent has no untapped mana to pay the {1} tax, preserving life total to execute the Doomsday win

annotations.description: KimiK2 Gramps had a Pyrogoyf ETB trigger (from casting/entering a second Pyrogoyf or from Fury's evoke) that deals damage equal to its power to any target. The opponent is at 8 life and Pyrogoyf's power is 5 (based on card types in graveyards). Instead of directing 5 damage at the opponent (putting them to 3 life, within lethal range), they targeted their own Pyrogoyf, effectively wasting the damage and killing their own creature. With the opponent at 8 life, directing damage to face is clearly superior, especially since Pyrogoyf was their primary attacker.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted their own Pyrogoyf with the 5 damage ETB trigger, destroying it.
annotations.betterLine: Target Kimi25 Analyst (the opponent) with the 5 damage, bringing them from 8 to 3 life, keeping the board pressure and putting the opponent in lethal range.

annotations.description: At 2 life, casting Force of Will (which costs 1 life via alternate cost) on Dark Ritual would put Analyst to 1 life, and wastes a hard counter on mana acceleration rather than the actual threat. More critically, with 2 Force of Wills in hand, Analyst can counter whatever payoff spell Gramps casts with the Dark Ritual mana. Dark Ritual itself doesn't threaten lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to counter Dark Ritual with Force of Will, paying 1 precious life at 2 life
annotations.betterLine: Let Dark Ritual resolve, keep both Force of Wills to counter the actual threatening spell that Gramps casts with the mana. At 2 life, preserving life total and saving counters for real threats is critical.

annotations.description: Kimi25 Analyst is at 2 life facing a Pyrogoyf and other threats, with Dark Ritual on the stack. Dark Ritual will give the opponent BBB mana, which could enable casting Blood Moon or other devastating spells. The opponent already has a Pyrogoyf that can attack for lethal next turn (with 3+ card types in graveyards giving it at least 3 power). Allowing Dark Ritual to resolve gives the opponent massive mana advantage to deploy more threats or disruption. With Daze and two Force of Wills in hand, countering Dark Ritual (via Daze returning an Island, or Force of Will exiling a blue card) would deny the opponent mana and potentially buy a critical turn. At 2 life, every turn matters and denying the opponent's mana development is crucial. The player appears to have cast Doomsday (it's in their graveyard) meaning they're on a Doomsday pile plan, but they have no draw spell in hand - they need to survive to draw into their pile. Letting Dark Ritual resolve when the opponent could use that mana to deploy a lethal threat or Blood Moon is game-losing.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Dark Ritual on the stack, allowing it to resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Counter Dark Ritual with Daze (returning an Island to hand) to deny the opponent BBB mana and prevent them from casting whatever follow-up they had planned. This preserves the two Force of Wills for protecting the combo or countering a more critical spell if needed.
